text.arabic_uthmani: ذَٰلِكَ وَمَن يُعَظِّمْ حُرُمَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌۭ لَّهُۥ عِندَ رَبِّهِۦ ۗ وَأُحِلَّتْ لَكُمُ ٱلْأَنْعَٰمُ إِلَّا مَا يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ ۖ فَٱجْتَنِبُوا۟ ٱلرِّجْسَ مِنَ ٱلْأَوْثَٰنِ وَٱجْتَنِبُوا۟ قَوْلَ ٱلزُّورِ

words.gloss_range: distal demonstrative closing the prior rite sequence while launching the next legal movement
words.prose: The demonstrative {{ar:ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:dhālika}}) is a compact closure marker rather than a new command. It points back to the completed rite sequence and turns that settled matter into the platform for the conditional promise, legal permission, and double avoidance command that follow.

topics.headline: demonstrative closure and launch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first word seals the prior rite block before the ayah moves into new law.
topics.reason: The reader notices that the first word seals the prior rite block before the ayah moves into new law.

words.gloss_range: resumptive connector joining prior closure to a fresh conditional statement
words.prose: The connector {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) keeps the ayah from making a hard break after the opening demonstrative. It resumes discourse so the sanctity condition belongs to the prior closure while still standing as a new legal principle.

topics.headline: resumption after closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a small connector preserving continuity while opening a fresh conditional statement.
topics.reason: The reader notices a small connector preserving continuity while opening a fresh conditional statement.

words.gloss_range: open conditional particle, whoever, governing the jussive protasis and universalizing the rule
words.prose: The particle {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) opens an unrestricted conditional frame. Because the following verb is jussive and the answer is introduced later, the ruling applies to whoever fulfills the condition rather than to a named group already in view.

topics.headline: whoever-condition architecture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sanctity claim is framed as an open rule for any qualifying person.
topics.reason: The reader notices that the sanctity claim is framed as an open rule for any qualifying person.

words.gloss_range: active treating-as-great of divine sanctities inside a conditional frame
words.root_gloss_range: greatness, weight, bone-like structural support, and derived active magnification; the local Form II selects enacted reverence, not a mere state of being great
words.prose: The verb {{ar:يُعَظِّمْ}} ({{tr:yuʿaẓẓim}}) makes honoring an action done toward sanctities, not a private feeling of greatness. Its Form II shape gives the act weight and intensification, while the jussive form keeps it inside the whoever-condition; the tightened middle consonant makes that weight audible. Coming after completed rites, the verb widens ritual completion into an enduring posture toward sanctities, and the same verb later returns with ritual signs in this surah (22:32).

topics.headline: active Form II honoring under condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that honoring sanctities is an enacted treatment of an object inside a conditional frame.
topics.reason: The reader notices that honoring sanctities is an enacted treatment of an object inside a conditional frame.

topics.headline: greatness and bone-weight pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels honoring as giving the sacred order weight and structure, while local grammar keeps the selected sense as active magnification.
topics.reason: The reader feels honoring as giving the sacred order weight and structure, while local grammar keeps the selected sense as active magnification.

topics.headline: same-surah magnification motif
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this exact honoring verb belongs to a repeated Hajj-law motif, especially with ritual signs in 22:32.
topics.reason: The reader notices that this exact honoring verb belongs to a repeated Hajj-law motif, especially with ritual signs in 22:32.

topics.headline: completed rites become general reverence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the movement from completed pilgrimage procedures into an enduring posture toward sanctities.
topics.reason: The reader notices the movement from completed pilgrimage procedures into an enduring posture toward sanctities.

topics.headline: geminated heaviness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the word’s tightened sound reinforce the weightiness of the act.
topics.reason: The reader hears the word’s tightened sound reinforce the weightiness of the act.

words.gloss_range: multiple inviolable sanctities as a divine construct object, protected and non-negotiable
words.root_gloss_range: sacredness, prohibition, protected precinct, inviolability, and forbiddenness; the local plural selects divinely bounded sanctities rather than mere customary prohibitions
words.prose: The plural construct {{ar:حُرُمَٰتِ}} ({{tr:ḥurumāti}}) makes the object of magnification a divine protected domain, definite through its annexation to the divine name rather than through custom. Its root field joins sacredness with non-violation, and the plural lets rites, limits, spaces, and moral boundaries gather under one object before the ayah turns to lawful release.

topics.headline: divine construct object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sanctities are definite because they are annexed to God, not because custom names them.
topics.reason: The reader notices that the sanctities are definite because they are annexed to God, not because custom names them.

topics.headline: protected sacred-boundary field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees sacredness and prohibition fused, so honoring sanctities means recognizing protected boundaries.
topics.reason: The reader sees sacredness and prohibition fused, so honoring sanctities means recognizing protected boundaries.

topics.headline: sacred restriction against lawful release
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah placing the protected-root field beside the lawful-release root in one legal taxonomy.
topics.reason: The reader notices the ayah placing the protected-root field beside the lawful-release root in one legal taxonomy.

topics.headline: ritual restriction widens to divine sanctities
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices personal rite completion opening into a broader divine protected domain.
topics.reason: The reader notices personal rite completion opening into a broader divine protected domain.

words.gloss_range: genitive divine proper name defining the sanctities as God’s domain
words.root_gloss_range: worship, divinity, awe, and the proper divine name; local grammar selects the divine possessor of the sanctities
words.prose: The divine name {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:allāhi}}) fixes the sanctities as God’s, not as social custom. Its genitive position gives the construct its definiteness and authority, and the worship-and-awe pressure of the name makes that authority devotional rather than merely possessive. The later shift to the relational Lord title personalizes the evaluation, while 22:32 and 22:40 extend the same divine-relation network.

topics.headline: divine name fixes authority
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sanctities are God’s domain, not negotiated social boundaries.
topics.reason: The reader notices that the sanctities are God’s domain, not negotiated social boundaries.

topics.headline: worship and awe pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the divine genitive as worship-authority, while local grammar keeps the proper name as the possessor of the sanctities.
topics.reason: The reader feels the divine genitive as worship-authority, while local grammar keeps the proper name as the possessor of the sanctities.

topics.headline: divine name and Lord title network
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah pairing God’s sanctities with the individual’s Lord, with 22:32 and 22:40 extending that divine-relation pattern.
topics.reason: The reader notices the ayah pairing God’s sanctities with the individual’s Lord, with 22:32 and 22:40 extending that divine-relation pattern.

words.gloss_range: conditional answer particle that visibly turns the honoring condition into its result
words.prose: The particle {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) is the hinge between condition and result. It marks the nominal answer as the payoff of honoring sanctities and makes the consequence arrive immediately rather than as a loose follow-up statement.

topics.headline: answer-particle hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the result clause as the explicit payoff of the honoring condition.
topics.reason: The reader notices the result clause as the explicit payoff of the honoring condition.

words.gloss_range: independent pronoun holding the predicate hinge and allowing act, agent, or matter reference
words.prose: The pronoun {{ar:هُوَ}} ({{tr:huwa}}) slows the answer before the predicate lands. Its independence lets the goodness be routed through the honoring act, the honoring person, or the whole matter, while still making the predication explicit.

topics.headline: explicit pronoun before predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the answer pause over what exactly is being predicated as good: the act, the actor, or the whole matter.
topics.reason: The reader notices the answer pause over what exactly is being predicated as good: the act, the actor, or the whole matter.

words.gloss_range: open good/better predicate whose comparison is measured in the Lord’s evaluative domain
words.root_gloss_range: goodness, betterment, choosing, and preferred value; the local predicate keeps both good and better pressure without naming a comparator
words.prose: The predicate {{ar:خَيْرٌ}} ({{tr:khayrun}}) gives the result an open evaluative force. With no stated comparator, the word can mean good and better, and the following phrase locates that value with the person’s Lord rather than with human preference. Its choice-goodness root pressure makes honoring sanctities the selected better outcome, and later surah uses around provision and doing good keep that value thread active.

topics.headline: open good-better predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the predicate’s comparison is left open rather than tied to a named human standard.
topics.reason: The reader notices the predicate’s comparison is left open rather than tied to a named human standard.

topics.headline: choice and goodness pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears goodness as the selected better outcome, while local syntax keeps the word as the predicate of the conditional result.
topics.reason: The reader hears goodness as the selected better outcome, while local syntax keeps the word as the predicate of the conditional result.

topics.headline: surah value thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices this promise joining later Hajj-surah value language around provision and doing good.
topics.reason: The reader notices this promise joining later Hajj-surah value language around provision and doing good.

words.gloss_range: benefactive preposition and suffix tying the good to the conditional actor
words.prose: The compact phrase {{ar:لَّهُۥ}} ({{tr:lahu}}) keeps the promised good personal. The preposition and suffix bind the benefit back to the whoever-condition, so the result is not an abstract good floating away from the actor.

topics.headline: benefit tied to the conditional actor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the good accrues personally to whoever honors, not to an abstract legal category.
topics.reason: The reader notices that the good accrues personally to whoever honors, not to an abstract legal category.

words.gloss_range: evaluative locus, at or with, locating the good in the Lord’s domain
words.root_gloss_range: presence, nearness, possession or station, and evaluative locus; local usage selects divine evaluative standing rather than physical location
words.prose: The adverb {{ar:عِندَ}} ({{tr:ʿinda}}) moves the comparison into an evaluative place. It is not merely spatial nearness; here it marks where the good counts, in the domain of the person’s Lord. The stable-station pressure behind the word helps the phrase feel like a recognized with-Lord evaluation construction rather than a loose metaphor.

topics.headline: good located with the Lord
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the comparison is measured in the Lord’s domain rather than by an unstated worldly scale.
topics.reason: The reader notices that the comparison is measured in the Lord’s domain rather than by an unstated worldly scale.

topics.headline: stable station pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels a stable evaluative station behind the phrase, while local usage keeps the sense evaluative rather than physically spatial.
topics.reason: The reader feels a stable evaluative station behind the phrase, while local usage keeps the sense evaluative rather than physically spatial.

topics.headline: recognized with-Lord formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the phrase participating in a recurring divine-evaluation construction.
topics.reason: The reader notices the phrase participating in a recurring divine-evaluation construction.

words.gloss_range: possessed Lord title individualizing divine evaluation for the conditional actor
words.root_gloss_range: lordship, mastery, ownership, sustaining, rearing, and governance; local usage selects the personal Lord as evaluator
words.prose: The title {{ar:رَبِّهِۦ}} ({{tr:rabbihi}}) is singular and suffixed, so the evaluator is personally related to each actor named by the conditional. Its root field keeps mastery and sustaining care together, making the judgment relational rather than detached. The same with-Lord construction recurs later in the surah (22:47), so this phrase anchors a broader evaluation thread.

topics.headline: possessed Lord title
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the evaluator is personally related to each conditional actor.
topics.reason: The reader notices that the evaluator is personally related to each conditional actor.

topics.headline: sustaining mastery in lordship
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees evaluation coming from the one who sustains and governs, not from an impersonal scale.
topics.reason: The reader sees evaluation coming from the one who sustains and governs, not from an impersonal scale.

topics.headline: Lord as evaluation anchor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices this phrase joining later with-Lord constructions, including 22:47.
topics.reason: The reader notices this phrase joining later with-Lord constructions, including 22:47.

words.gloss_range: resumptive connector shifting from conditional promise to legal declaration
words.prose: The connector {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) begins a new legal sentence without severing it from the sanctity principle. It pivots the ayah from whoever honors to what has been made lawful for the addressed community.

topics.headline: promise-to-permission transition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah shifting from a conditional promise into a concrete legal declaration while remaining connected to the sanctity principle.
topics.reason: The reader notices the ayah shifting from a conditional promise into a concrete legal declaration while remaining connected to the sanctity principle.

words.gloss_range: passive conferred lawfulness, already established and immediately bounded by exception
words.root_gloss_range: loosening, untying, settling, and making lawful; the local passive Form IV selects conferred legal release from restriction
words.prose: The passive verb {{ar:أُحِلَّتْ}} ({{tr:uḥillat}}) foregrounds the livestock as made lawful while leaving the permitting agent unstated but contextually divine. The root’s loosening image makes lawfulness feel like released restriction, and the nearby exception keeps that release bounded by revelation. Coming after completed restriction-removal rites, the legal loosening echoes the boundary movement from ritual completion into permitted access.

topics.headline: passive conferred lawfulness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that lawful access is a granted status, with livestock foregrounded and the permitting agent left reverently implicit.
topics.reason: The reader notices that lawful access is a granted status, with livestock foregrounded and the permitting agent left reverently implicit.

topics.headline: loosening as permission
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels permission as restriction released, while local Form IV passive keeps the sense as conferred lawfulness.
topics.reason: The reader feels permission as restriction released, while local Form IV passive keeps the sense as conferred lawfulness.

topics.headline: permission immediately bounded
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the legal permission is structurally incomplete until the recited exception narrows it.
topics.reason: The reader notices that the legal permission is structurally incomplete until the recited exception narrows it.

topics.headline: ritual completion and legal loosening converge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the movement from completed restriction-removal rites to a stated legal release.
topics.reason: The reader notices the movement from completed restriction-removal rites to a stated legal release.

words.gloss_range: second-person plural beneficiary phrase assigning lawful access to the addressed community
words.prose: The phrase {{ar:لَكُمُ}} ({{tr:lakumu}}) turns the legal status toward the addressed community. After the individualized benefit earlier in the ayah, this second-person plural form makes the permission communal and direct.

topics.headline: community receives lawful access
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from an individual conditional beneficiary to a directly addressed community receiving permission.
topics.reason: The reader notices the shift from an individual conditional beneficiary to a directly addressed community receiving permission.

words.gloss_range: recognized livestock class as the foregrounded lawful patient, with blessing and provision pressure
words.root_gloss_range: livestock, blessing, ease, comfort, and bounty; the local noun selects the lawful animal class while retaining favor semantics
words.prose: The noun {{ar:ٱلْأَنْعَٰمُ}} ({{tr:al-anʿāmu}}) names the known livestock class as the thing made lawful. Its root family ties animals to blessing and provision, so the ruling concerns embodied favor, not bare consumption; the formula recalls the lawful-livestock exception in 5:1 and connects the permission clause to the surah’s sacrificial animal economy.

topics.headline: known livestock class foregrounded
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the livestock class as the lawful patient of the passive ruling, not as an indefinite set of animals.
topics.reason: The reader notices the livestock class as the lawful patient of the passive ruling, not as an indefinite set of animals.

topics.headline: livestock as embodied bounty
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the permitted animals as provision and favor, while local usage keeps the word as the livestock class.
topics.reason: The reader feels the permitted animals as provision and favor, while local usage keeps the word as the livestock class.

topics.headline: lawful livestock formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the near-formulaic echo of 5:1 and the link to the surah’s sacrificial animal economy.
topics.reason: The reader notices the near-formulaic echo of 5:1 and the link to the surah’s sacrificial animal economy.

words.gloss_range: exception particle cutting back a general permission through a connected exclusion
words.prose: The particle {{ar:إِلَّا}} ({{tr:illā}}) prevents the permission clause from closing as unlimited. It keeps the excluded category inside the livestock-law domain while removing it from lawful access.

topics.headline: exception limits permission
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that lawful access is bounded from inside the permission clause rather than added later as a separate warning.
topics.reason: The reader notices that lawful access is bounded from inside the permission clause rather than added later as a separate warning.

words.gloss_range: open relative pronoun whose referent is specified by the recited clause
words.prose: The pronoun {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) does not name the excluded animals itself. It delays the referent until the following passive recitation supplies the authoritative content of the exception.

topics.headline: open relative exception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the exception referent being deferred until recitation supplies its content.
topics.reason: The reader notices the exception referent being deferred until recitation supplies its content.

words.gloss_range: passive ongoing recitation that specifies the legal exception as binding revelation
words.root_gloss_range: following, reciting, successive reading, and being led after something; local passive usage selects recitation that must be followed as legal specification
words.prose: The verb {{ar:يُتْلَىٰ}} ({{tr:yutlā}}) makes recitation the mechanism that bounds permission. Its passive imperfect keeps the focus on authoritative content continually encountered, and the root’s follow-recitation range lets hearing the exception become following it. The same lawfulness-plus-recitation pattern recalls 5:1, where general livestock permission is bounded by what is recited.

topics.headline: passive ongoing recitation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the exception is anchored in authoritative recitation rather than an itemized local list.
topics.reason: The reader notices that the exception is anchored in authoritative recitation rather than an itemized local list.

topics.headline: reciting and following converge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses that hearing the exception requires following it, while local grammar keeps recitation as the selected sense.
topics.reason: The reader senses that hearing the exception requires following it, while local grammar keeps recitation as the selected sense.

topics.headline: lawfulness-plus-recitation formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the 5:1 legal formula reappearing, where general permission is bounded by what is recited.
topics.reason: The reader notices the 5:1 legal formula reappearing, where general permission is bounded by what is recited.

words.gloss_range: upon-you phrase marking the community as recipients under recited obligation
words.prose: The phrase {{ar:عَلَيْكُمْ}} ({{tr:ʿalaykum}}) places the addressees under the recited specification. The upon-sense carries direction and obligation, preparing the same audience to receive the direct imperative that follows.

topics.headline: recitation falls upon the audience
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the community receiving recitation is the same community about to be commanded.
topics.reason: The reader notices that the community receiving recitation is the same community about to be commanded.

words.gloss_range: resultative particle turning bounded law into practical avoidance command
words.prose: The particle {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) shifts the ayah from declaration to command. It draws out the practical consequence of sanctity, lawful permission, and recited exception: the community must now create distance from the named contaminant.

topics.headline: legal consequence becomes imperative
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the particle turning bounded legal declaration into direct practical avoidance.
topics.reason: The reader notices the particle turning bounded legal declaration into direct practical avoidance.

words.gloss_range: plural imperative of deliberate self-distancing from contamination
words.root_gloss_range: side, flank, separation, avoidance, and ritual impurity; local Form VIII selects volitional self-positioning away from the object
words.prose: The imperative {{ar:ٱجْتَنِبُوا۟}} ({{tr:ijtanibū}}) addresses the community directly and commands more than passive non-use. Its Form VIII and side-root pressure picture moral obedience as placing oneself aside from contamination, with compact consonantal pressure reinforcing the deliberate cut away. The same form returns at word 27 to make speech avoidance parallel to idol-contamination, and related avoidance formulas include 5:90 and 39:17.

topics.headline: direct Form VIII command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices avoidance as deliberate self-positioning by the addressed community, not passive non-use.
topics.reason: The reader notices avoidance as deliberate self-positioning by the addressed community, not passive non-use.

topics.headline: side-distance and impurity pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels moral action as moving one’s side away from contamination.
topics.reason: The reader feels moral action as moving one’s side away from contamination.

topics.headline: contamination-command parallels
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the idol-contamination command aligning with other Quranic avoidance formulas, including 5:90 and 39:17.
topics.reason: The reader notices the idol-contamination command aligning with other Quranic avoidance formulas, including 5:90 and 39:17.

topics.headline: first half of paired avoidance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the first imperative opening a two-command structure completed by the repeated imperative at word 27.
topics.reason: The reader sees the first imperative opening a two-command structure completed by the repeated imperative at word 27.

topics.headline: compact distancing sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the compact consonantal pressure reinforce the deliberate cut away from the object.
topics.reason: The reader hears the compact consonantal pressure reinforce the deliberate cut away from the object.

words.gloss_range: definite impurity or abomination as the direct object of commanded avoidance
words.root_gloss_range: physical filth, moral abomination, contamination, and related punitive impurity fields; local usage selects idol-related impurity as an avoided object
words.prose: The noun {{ar:ٱلرِّجْسَ}} ({{tr:al-rijsa}}) is the object that must be avoided, and the following phrase specifies its idol-related instance. The word carries physical-filth pressure into the moral and ritual field, aligning this prohibition with the contamination label used in 5:90. That contamination field then converges with the closing speech-deviation field, so polluted worship and crooked speech become parallel contaminants.

topics.headline: definite avoided impurity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices impurity as the direct object of avoidance before the idol phrase specifies it.
topics.reason: The reader notices impurity as the direct object of avoidance before the idol phrase specifies it.

topics.headline: filth transferred to idolatry
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels physical contamination language transferred into moral and ritual idolatry.
topics.reason: The reader feels physical contamination language transferred into moral and ritual idolatry.

topics.headline: marked contamination label
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the uncommon impurity label linking this idol prohibition to broader contamination contexts such as 5:90.
topics.reason: The reader notices the uncommon impurity label linking this idol prohibition to broader contamination contexts such as 5:90.

topics.headline: polluted worship paired with crooked speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah preparing to pair idol contamination with false speech as parallel contaminants.
topics.reason: The reader notices the ayah preparing to pair idol contamination with false speech as parallel contaminants.

words.gloss_range: prepositional specification linking impurity to idols, with explanatory and partitive scope pressure
words.prose: The preposition {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) binds the abstract impurity to the concrete idol class. Whether heard as explanatory or partitive, it prevents impurity and idols from becoming two unrelated objects and controls the scope of the avoidance phrase.

topics.headline: preposition specifying impurity by idols
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the particle controlling whether idols are the impurity itself, a source of it, or a subset specification.
topics.reason: The reader notices the particle controlling whether idols are the impurity itself, a source of it, or a subset specification.

words.gloss_range: definite plural idols as the specified source or identity of impurity, broader than one carved image
words.root_gloss_range: set-up or fixed worshipped object, idol, and false object of devotion; local plural selects the recognized idol class
words.prose: The noun {{ar:ٱلْأَوْثَٰنِ}} ({{tr:al-awthāni}}) names idols as a known plural class governed by the preceding preposition. Its root pressure makes the false object feel fixed or set up, broader than a single carved image, and its rare Quranic cluster with 29:17 and 29:25 turns this local legal avoidance into part of a marked anti-idol vocabulary. The movement from the legitimate sacred center to fixed false centers is reinforced by the word’s heavy closing sound texture.

topics.headline: known idol class under the preposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices idols as the specified genitive class, not as a second direct object.
topics.reason: The reader notices idols as the specified genitive class, not as a second direct object.

topics.headline: fixed false object pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels idol worship as attachment to fixed false objects, while local usage keeps the noun as the plural idol class.
topics.reason: The reader feels idol worship as attachment to fixed false objects, while local usage keeps the noun as the plural idol class.

topics.headline: rare idol-prohibition cluster
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the rare plural joining the Abrahamic rejection passages in 29:17 and 29:25.
topics.reason: The reader notices the rare plural joining the Abrahamic rejection passages in 29:17 and 29:25.

topics.headline: true sacred center against false fixed centers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the movement from legitimate sacred center to rejected false centers.
topics.reason: The reader notices the movement from legitimate sacred center to rejected false centers.

topics.headline: heavy fixed-object texture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the closing sound texture reinforce the sense of fixed objects needing avoidance.
topics.reason: The reader hears the closing sound texture reinforce the sense of fixed objects needing avoidance.

words.gloss_range: coordinating connector launching a second full avoidance command
words.prose: The connector {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) does not simply add a second object to the first command. Because the imperative is repeated after it, the particle coordinates two full commands and gives false speech its own command frame.

topics.headline: coordination of two full commands
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that false speech receives its own command frame rather than trailing as another object of the first command.
topics.reason: The reader notices that false speech receives its own command frame rather than trailing as another object of the first command.

words.gloss_range: repeated plural imperative applying deliberate avoidance to false speech
words.root_gloss_range: side, flank, separation, avoidance, and ritual impurity; the second local use reapplies the same Form VIII self-distancing to a speech object
words.prose: The repeated imperative {{ar:ٱجْتَنِبُوا۟}} ({{tr:ijtanibū}}) gives the speech phrase direct command force. The same avoidance morphology used for idol-contamination is now applied to utterance, so the ayah closes by making verbal falsehood a parallel object of self-distancing.

topics.headline: second direct avoidance command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices false speech receiving independent imperative force.
topics.reason: The reader notices false speech receiving independent imperative force.

topics.headline: side-distance applied to speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the same self-distancing discipline transferred from material contamination to utterance.
topics.reason: The reader feels the same self-distancing discipline transferred from material contamination to utterance.

topics.headline: imperative reprise equates the targets
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated imperative equating idol-contamination and false speech as parallel avoidance classes.
topics.reason: The reader notices the repeated imperative equating idol-contamination and false speech as parallel avoidance classes.

words.gloss_range: accusative construct speech as the direct object, intrinsically defined by falsehood
words.root_gloss_range: saying, speech, utterance, and derived fabrication of speech; the local construct selects speech characterized by falsehood
words.prose: The noun {{ar:قَوْلَ}} ({{tr:qawla}}) is both the object of avoidance and the construct head defined by falsehood. It holds act and product together, so the command targets producing false utterance and accepting the uttered falsehood as speech, while the wider fabrication branch sharpens that danger without replacing the local construct sense. The phrase forms a marked false-speech pair, contrasts with legitimate formulaic speech over livestock in 22:36, mirrors the idol-contamination object as the second half of the double prohibition, and lands with compact closing cadence.

words.prose: The genitive noun {{ar:ٱلزُّورِ}} ({{tr:al-zūri}}) completes the construct phrase by making falsehood the domain to which the speech belongs. Its deviation-root pressure makes the false speech feel bent away from truth, while the abstract noun keeps the focus on the false quality rather than naming a falsifier. The term also joins broader falsehood contexts, including witnessed falsehood in 25:72, and its final sound arc leaves speech ethics as the ayah’s closing residue.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence magnifies God's hurumat, calls that good for the person, and locates the good near the person's Lord.
baseline_models.mechanism: Magnification is not mere admiration: it increases the operative weight of a protected right so that it governs conduct. The resulting good is relational and formative because it is assessed in the near presence of the Lord who cultivates and completes.

activation_trace.role: Honor and inviolability make magnification the act of granting protected things operative weight.
Protected right, pledge, and dignity supply what must not be squandered or breached.
Nearness and presence turn the promised good into value assessed before the Lord.
Cultivation and completion make that assessment formative rather than merely locative.

changed_reading.before: Respecting divine prohibitions earns a benefit.
changed_reading.after: The person actively enlarges the governing force of protected divine rights, and that boundary-work becomes formative good in the Lord's presence.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Livestock are made lawful, except for what is recited to the audience.
baseline_models.mechanism: Lawfulness loosens a restriction, but the following recitation retains an attached exception. Permission therefore operates as a bounded release whose limit remains audibly renewable rather than as an unqualified transfer of control.

activation_trace.role: Dissolution of a ban supplies the legal opening rather than unrestricted ownership.
The livestock branch fixes the concrete resource over which release is granted.
Following in sequence makes the recited exception remain attached to and delimit the permission.

changed_reading.before: Livestock are generally permitted, with a previously known list of exceptions.
changed_reading.after: A prohibition is untied only within a continuing recited sequence, so permission remains bounded by speech that follows and delimits it.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The same repeated command to keep aside governs both the contaminant from idols and bent speech.
baseline_models.mechanism: Repeated side-distancing joins a material cult object and a verbal production into one decontamination protocol. Idols can stain and confuse by fixing worship onto an object; speech can depart from its line and be pre-shaped into falsehood. Both channels must be moved outside operative adjacency.

activation_trace.role: Active distancing and removal to the side supply one spatial operation for both prohibitions.
Staining, mixing contamination gives the cult object a transmissible effect rather than making it inert.
The worshipped image supplies the material channel onto which devotion is wrongly fixed.
Speech brought into audible expression supplies the second, socially mobile channel.
Deviation from a straight line makes false speech a directional distortion.
Pre-shaping and beautifying discourse shows how verbal distortion can be deliberately manufactured.

changed_reading.before: Avoid idols and avoid lying as two adjacent prohibitions.
changed_reading.after: Create the same operative distance from two contaminating media: fixed cult objects and manufactured, direction-bending speech.

context_deltas.mechanism: The sacred precinct is made equal for the settled devotee and the outsider, while deviation within it is threatened. This turns a protected boundary from an exclusionary enclosure into a right of non-skewed access whose sanctity is violated by monopolization or diversion.

activation_trace.role: Protected right and inviolable claim anchor the revision in the focus plural hurumat.
Equality between two parties makes access, not exclusion, the sacred spatial norm.
Deviation from the straight or rightful line supplies the mechanism by which access is skewed.

structural_cues: 22:25 places the sacred mosque, equality of resident and outsider, and threatened deviation in one construction.
The focus follows this access warning within the same ritual sequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies equal access and punishable deviation at one sacred site; I extend that access logic to the focus plural hurumat. A live alternative is that 22:25 regulates only the mosque and does not generalize every inviolability.

changed_reading.before: Magnifying sacred limits means personally refraining from crossing them.
changed_reading.after: Magnifying sacred limits also means preserving their protected, non-exclusionary access structure and resisting uses that bend it toward private control.

context_deltas.mechanism: The livestock are first received as apportioned provision, then move through two distinct acts: eating and causing another to eat, with the poor named as recipient. Lawful release thus opens a circulation path rather than ending in private consumption.

activation_trace.role: Removal of restriction anchors the contextual change in the focus grant of lawfulness.
Livestock wealth is the resource whose lawful movement is being traced.
Apportioned gift makes the animals received provision rather than self-originating property.
Personal eating supplies the first permitted destination of the resource.
Feeding another turns permission outward into an enacted transfer.
Material need identifies the transfer's socially exposed recipient.

structural_cues: 22:28 names provision, the same livestock class, eating, feeding, and the poor in one ordered sequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a provision-to-eating-to-feeding sequence; I read that sequence as the social direction of the focus permission. A live alternative is that feeding is a neighboring rite rather than an intrinsic condition of lawfulness.

changed_reading.before: The livestock clause grants a bounded permission to consume.
changed_reading.after: The bounded permission initiates a distributive circuit: received provision becomes lawful eating and obligatory attention to another's hunger.

context_deltas.mechanism: Magnifying ritual signs is located in the protected core of the heart, and the sacrificial materials are explicitly denied arrival while taqwa does arrive. Magnification therefore routes material practice into inward protective orientation and guided recognition, not material transfer to God.

activation_trace.role: Honor and inviolability anchor the contextual account of what magnification does.
Placing oneself in protection makes taqwa an active inward boundary.
The core or kernel locates ritual magnification in the person's interior center.
Contrasted arrival distinguishes what can reach the divine relation from what cannot.
Literal flesh supplies one material that is denied relational arrival.
Literal blood supplies the other material that is denied relational arrival.
Enlarging something in the chest turns magnification into an inward response to guidance.

structural_cues: 22:32 repeats magnification and explicitly derives it from heart-taqwa.
22:37 contrasts flesh and blood with taqwa, then commands magnification because of guidance.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated magnification, heart-taqwa, failed material arrival, and guided magnification; I treat these as the mechanism behind the focus promise of good near the Lord. A live alternative is that signs and hurumat retain distinct scopes despite the repeated verb.

changed_reading.before: Large outward respect for sacred things wins divine approval.
changed_reading.after: Outward rite matters by forming an inward protective orientation that reaches the divine relation; its flesh, blood, and display do not themselves cross that distance.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate association simile converts failed exclusive orientation into a sequence of uncontrolled motion: fall, seizure, wind-driven descent, and remote deposition. Side-distancing in the focus now functions as preventive trajectory control, keeping material and verbal deviations from taking over the person's direction.

activation_trace.role: Deliberate distancing supplies the preventive action that preserves direction.
Directional bending anchors the model in the focus prohibition of false speech.
Association supplies the initial loss of exclusive orientation.
Noisy, unstable falling converts deviation into loss of self-directed motion.
Swift seizure shows an outside force capturing the fallen person's path.
Descent into an abyss supplies the vertical vector of disorientation.
Extreme remoteness supplies the endpoint produced when direction is surrendered.

structural_cues: 22:31 immediately follows the paired avoidance commands with a kinetic simile for association.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the fall sequence for association; I let it explain why active side-distance is needed and extend the directional risk to the paired bent-speech command. A live alternative is that the simile activates idols alone and says nothing about false speech.

changed_reading.before: Avoidance means refusing two forbidden items.
changed_reading.after: Avoidance is active control of adjacency and direction before a cult object or bent utterance captures the person's trajectory and deposits it far from its center.

context_deltas.mechanism: People are expelled for one truthful utterance, while reciprocal defense prevents demolition of multiple places where God's name is voiced. The negative command against bent speech thus acquires a positive public complement: truthful naming and the spaces that sustain it require protection.

activation_trace.role: Audible utterance anchors the change in the focus command concerning speech.
Departure from the truthful line identifies the negative speech form to be excluded.
A voiced confession supplies the truthful speech whose social cost exposes the positive stakes.
Pushing harm aside turns protection from a private attitude into public counterforce.
Building collapse supplies the material consequence that defense prevents.
Mention flowing on the tongue connects protected buildings to sustained truthful naming.

structural_cues: 22:40 makes a truthful statement the sole stated cause of expulsion.
The same ayah links defense to the survival of several kinds of worship place where God's name is mentioned.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies persecuted truthful speech and defended naming-spaces; I infer that avoiding false speech has a constructive public counterpart in protecting truthful utterance. A live alternative is that the focus command remains individual while 22:40 concerns only communal defense.

changed_reading.before: Avoid false speech by keeping one's own words accurate.
changed_reading.after: Speech integrity also has public infrastructure: bent utterance is excluded while truthful naming and the diverse spaces that carry it are actively defended.

context_deltas.mechanism: A later transmission scene contains recitation, hostile casting into it, removal of the insertion, and firm establishment of signs. The focus exception by what is recited, beside the command to avoid manufactured speech, therefore reads as an integrity-sensitive channel rather than self-authenticating sound.

activation_trace.role: Following recitation anchors the model in the channel that delimits lawful livestock.
Deliberate pre-shaping of discourse supplies the focus warning against manufactured verbal content.
Recitation read and placed in sequence supplies the transmission surface under pressure.
Casting something down supplies the intrusive action against the transmission surface.
Removal followed by replacement supplies a corrective stage rather than passive reception.
Firm establishment and exactness supply the authenticated endpoint of the correction.

structural_cues: 22:52 orders recitation, hostile casting, removal, and establishment in one transmission sequence.
The focus places recited legal limitation and avoidance of manufactured speech in the same ayah.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an insertion-and-correction process in prophetic transmission; I use it to make the focus recited exception integrity-sensitive. A live alternative is that 22:52 addresses a distinct prophetic event and should not qualify the dietary recitation in 22:30.

changed_reading.before: Whatever is recited functions as a transparent list of dietary exceptions.
changed_reading.after: Recitation is an authoritative but guarded transmission channel: what binds must survive the distinction between following revelation and cast, manufactured speech.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the non-primary fixedness branch of the idol noun and then reverses it through a late parable. It remains anchored in the focus word for idols, while 22:73 explicitly tests invoked beings' capacity and finds them unable to create or recover even a fly. Render it as an exploratory lexical reversal, not as a replacement definition of idol.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus calls for distance from the contaminant arising from idols; the idol root also carries an image of strength and fixed endurance.

activation_trace.role: Apparent strength and fixed endurance supply the idol's claim to stable agency.
Creative origination supplies the first agency test that the invoked beings fail.
The literal fly supplies the minimal creature that exposes the pretended strength.
Failed extraction from another's grasp supplies the second agency test.
Explicit lack of strength overturns the idol's branch image of fixed power.

changed_reading.after: Idols are also claims of durable agency whose fixed facade is experimentally collapsed by inability to originate or retrieve even the smallest life.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because a literal animal side reactivates a command normally read as an idiom for avoidance. It remains valid as a same-root spatial activation inside the livestock ritual sequence. Render it only as embodied choreography and adjacency management, never as a claim that the avoidance verb literally means an animal flank.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The repeated focus verb creates side-distance from both cult contamination and false speech.

activation_trace.role: Moving something away to the side supplies the focus's repeated distancing action.
Alignment on a level row supplies deliberate bodily positioning before the sacrifice.
Falling supplies the transition that makes the animals' sides operationally salient.
The literal bodily flank re-materializes the spatial image carried by the focus avoidance commands.

changed_reading.before: Avoidance is an abstract rejection of wrong objects and words.
changed_reading.after: Avoidance carries an embodied spatial resonance: in a ritual field organized by rows, falling bodies, and exposed flanks, contamination and bent speech are deliberately kept beyond one's operative side.

strongest_changes: Hurumat became protected access and rights, not merely privately observed taboos.
Livestock lawfulness became a circulation from apportioned provision through eating to feeding the poor.
Magnification became heart-level protective orientation because flesh and blood do not themselves reach the divine relation.
False speech and recited exception became a broader integrity architecture joining truthful public naming with guarded transmission.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet made one ayah operate simultaneously as legal topology, resource circulation, ritual interiorization, trajectory control, and speech infrastructure without dissolving those readings into one final interpretation.
remaining_uncertainties: The equal-access mechanism may belong specifically to the sacred mosque rather than every item in the plural hurumat.
The recitation-under-insertion scene may be too remote or domain-distinct to qualify the dietary recitation directly.
The falling simile explicitly targets association; its extension to the paired false-speech command remains inferential.
The fixed-idol and animal-flank outliers are lexical resonances, not claims of primary word meaning.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Magnification means maintaining protected boundaries.** `ع ظ م B001/B010` supplies greatness and honored standing; `ح ر م B003/B006` protected bounds and inviolable claim; `ح ل ل B003` removal of prohibition. Permission and exception follow reverence. I infer that honoring sacred limits requires discriminating what is opened from what remains barred. Magnification therefore reads as disciplined boundary-keeping, not indiscriminate severity.
2. **Idol-taint and false speech share a sideward mechanism.** Repeated `ج ن ب B003` commands keeping aside; `ر ج س B001/B005` is taint and confused entanglement; `و ث ن B001/B002` a worshipped fixed idol; `ز و ر B001/B002` deviation and invalid speech. I infer that material fixation and verbal falsification both divert orientation from its proper center. Their paired avoidance reads as cleansing both object-world and speech-world of the same deviation.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 22:72 later made false orientation visible on hostile faces and in attempted assault, showing how deviant speech passes from utterance into embodied force.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Sanctity operates by discriminating boundaries, not blanket taboo.** Fixed `يُعَظِّم` activates `ع ظ م:B001` (magnifying or venerating), `حُرُمَات` activates `ح ر م:B006` (inviolable claim, pact, and respect), and `أُحِلَّت` activates `ح ل ل:B003` (removal of prohibition). The permitted livestock field is narrowed by what follows in recitation (`ت ل و:B001`, following in sequence), while two repeated `ٱجْتَنِبُوا` use `ج ن ب:B003` (keeping aside) against `ر ج س:B001` (tainting defilement), `و ث ن:B001` (worshipped idol), and `ز و ر:B002` (false speech). `22:29` supplied fulfilled commitments and `22:31` shows the consequence of partnership. The packet supplies permission, transmitted exception, and exclusions; I infer a legal sorting mechanism. Honoring limits means keeping distinct what is open, conditioned, and contaminating.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later `22:31` dramatizes what failure to keep these distinctions does to orientation, while `22:32` corrects reverence from mere prohibition toward heart-generated valuation of signs.

baseline.text: İşte böyle. Kim Allah'ın dokunulmaz kıldıklarına saygı gösterirse bu, Rabbi katında kendisi için hayırlıdır. Size okunanlar dışında hayvanlar helal kılındı. Öyleyse putların pisliğinden ve yalan sözden kaçının.

findings.text: Allah'ın yasaklarına saygı, her şeyi yasaklamak değil, korunan sınırlarla helal bırakılan alanları dikkatle ayırt etmektir.
Putların kiri ile yalan sözün birlikte anılması, bedensel yön sapmasıyla sözdeki sapmayı aynı uzak durma buyruğunda birleştirir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi büyüklük ve gücü çekirdek anlam olarak verir; değer ve mevki büyüklüğünü de buna bağlar. Bir şeyi büyük sayma, büyütme, yüceltme ve saygıyla ululama anlamları ise aynı çekirdeğin türemiş ya da kalıplaşmış gerçekleşmeleridir ve yalın anlamla bir tutulmamalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, fiziksel ya da soyut büyüklük ve gücü kapsar; çoğunluk, kemik, felaket ve yerilen kibir anlamlarını kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın büyüklük ve güç çekirdeğini türemiş büyütme, yüceltme, büyük sayma ve ünlem kalıbından ayrı tutar.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin boyut, güç, değer ya da mevki bakımından büyük olmasıdır; türemiş kullanımlarda bir şeyi büyük saymayı, büyütüp görkemli göstermeyi veya saygıyla yüceltmeyi anlatır.

facets.statement: Bir varlık ya da durum boyut, güç, değer veya mevki bakımından büyük ve üstün olabilir.
Türemiş biçimler bir şeyi büyütme, görkemli gösterme, büyük sayma ya da saygıyla yüceltme eylemini bildirir.
Belirli bir ünlem kalıbı, övgü ya da yergi bağlamında bir özelliğin büyüklüğüne şaşmayı anlatır.
